result.summary: No-ship: two prescribed report sentences contradict reproducible collector outcomes. No separate material machinery findings; the coverage boundary, stale-pointer residual and absent heading ownership match the code.

findings.title: Deferred counts can promise retries for permanently memoized oversized sessions
findings.body: Capacity and deadline stops classify the entire unvisited remainder before checking oversized memos (scratch.js:91–105), while preserving those memos. I reproduced an admitted session followed by a memoized oversized session: either stop counted the latter as deferred, with oversized=0. On the following run it was skipped from its memo without parsing. The prescribed promise that these sessions “will be retried on the next run” therefore misrepresents a persistent exclusion as temporary. B4/B5's assertion that these sessions have no ledger record is also false for this case.
findings.recommendation: Describe B4/B5 as sessions left unvisited when the input/time limit stopped collection, without guaranteeing a next-run retry. State that existing oversized memos may survive within either remainder. Update the wording mirrors and add fixtures covering preserved memos behind both stops.

findings.title: Re-quarantined sessions are falsely reported as skipped for the first time
findings.body: A previously quarantined file whose fingerprint changes is selected again (ledger.js:242). If it remains over the ceiling or parsing fails, it enters newlyQuarantined again (scratch.js:58,111). I reproduced this alongside an admitted session, so the proposed report would print “skipped for the first time” for a session already quarantined previously. Criterion 4(c) explicitly requires this classification but never reconciles it with the rendered historical claim.
findings.recommendation: Remove the first-ever claim from B1 and its definition; describe this run's quarantine decision instead. Update every byte-exact mirror and assert the resulting report wording for criterion 4(c)'s re-quarantine case.
